To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the loco-regional control of small-cell lung carcinoma is improved by increasing the radiation-dose to greater than or equal 50 Gy.

(1) the probability of locoregional failure is significantly lower with higher radiation doses; (2) the probability of death from lung carcinoma is significantly lower with lower radiation doses; (3) there is a trade-off between locoregional and distant failure; and (4) the probability of survival is significantly higher with higher radiation doses.
the probability of locoregional tumor control in patients with limited stage small-cell carcinoma is significantly improved by the use of radiation-doses of greater than or equal 45 Gy.
